steps.text: Beat egg whites in a large glass, metal, or ceramic bowl with an electric mixer at high speed until foamy.
Gradually add sugar and lemon extract; continue to beat on high speed until thickened.
Use to pipe or decorate cookies.

raw_recipe.headline: Royal Icing
raw_recipe.description: This royal icing recipe makes a sweet white icing that dries quickly, making it perfect for decorating gingerbread houses and holiday cookies.
raw_recipe.name: Royal Icing

Gradually add sugar and lemon extract; continue to beat on high speed until thickened.
Use to pipe or decorate cookies.

review.reviewBody: This recipe is great! I dries hard like it should. But i actually added another cup of powdered sugar to get the consistency i wanted. (as is it comes out runny) I also added a tsp of vanilla instead of the lemon, and it still came out good. I will definately use this recipe again and often!

Great glue and icing for our gingerbread house!! I read other reviewers thoughts and used 3 large egg whites and 4 cups of confectioners sugar, 1 tsp vanilla and a dash or two of cream of tartar. PERFECTION. And the first time too!! (to pasteurize egg whites- slowly stir the egg whites with a whisk over a double boiler until they are warm to the touch but not too long!!)

This recipe does super!! Definitely sift your sugar before mixing! I used 1/2 cup of pasteurized egg whites and 2 drops of almond emulsion instead of lemon. I mixed up everything by hand first, then put it into the mixer for 5 minutes to soft peak. Then, for piping outlines I used it straight. For flooding I added a teaspoon of water. I used gel food coloring. I agree with the comments that if your consistency is wrong then you did not beat it long enough. Cover your bowl with a damp cloth when not in use because the icing will dry quickly if you do not cover it.

This worked well for me. I pasteurized my own egg whites by whisking them with half the sugar over a double boiler until the mixture reached 160°F (about 7-8 minutes). Then I removed it from the heat and beat in the rest of the sugar and flavoring until it reached the desired consistency.

I've used this recipe a lot and love it. We've used it to decorate sugar cookies for both Halloween and Christmas and also for gingerbread men and houses. I followed the recipe exactly for the sugar cookies. For the gingerbread, I used vanilla instead of lemon extract. Just for personal taste preferences. :)

I've found that to get it strong enough to hold heavy gingerbread houses, I needed to let the mixer go for about 6 minutes after I added the sugar to the eggs. For "flooding" a sugar cookie, it needed to mix for more like 4 minutes. If it's coming out too thin and taking a while to get hard, it's because it needs to mix longer. 

As others said, it's best to keep what you aren't using in a ziplock bag or another airtight container or it will get hard.

Very easy to do the little outline and then fill in. I used vanilla instead of the lemon. I used this Royal Icing recipe with the "Best Rolled Sugar Cookies" recipe on here and the kids and grand kids like them better than store bought or bakery ones. I frosted a lot more than was in the picture and still had some icing left over.

This recipe worked well for decorating gingerbread cookies. Mixing a long time on high speed is the key to thickening the frosting. I used 1 teasppon of vanilla (instead of lemon extract) and added 1/2 teaspoon of cream of tartar. “Adding a small amount of cream of tartar when you're beating egg whites—usually 1/8 teaspoon per egg white—speeds up the creation of foam and helps stabilize the structure of those miniscule air bubbles you're whipping up.” [from Allrecipes]

It worked for its intended purpose but I found that it need more confectioners sugar than it says. With the amount it says, it is too runny, but adding more gave me the right consistency I needed. Over all it worked and tasted great.

followed the recipe, but swapped vanilla in for the lemon. OUTSTANDING. It was great! I thinned it with a little water for medium consistency. It dried beautifully and tastes delicious. it was the perfect icing for gingerbread cookies.

Fellas!!! You may think the ingredients look to little. They’re not!!! 1 batch is more than enough to make 3 different colors and coat a full batch of sugar cookies. Forget about that two different consistencies nonsense, make one batch and then put it in 3 bowls add some color and then grab one of those brushes you use for bbq sauce and brush that sweet sugar sauce on. Add sprinkles after if you want. Enjoy!!

Just tried this recipe for googly eyes. Perfection! I just used the whites of one egg as I didn't need a lot of icing. I added powdered sugar and a few drops of lemon juice until I reached the proper consistency. I probably needed less than a cup of powdered sugar. As others suggested I mixed it for several minutes. The eyes came out great!

We use this recipe every holiday season to "glue" our gingerbread houses together and decorate them. The thickness of the icing can be adjusted to make it thinner or thicker for whatever purpose you need it for. . .mortar or decoration. ;)
No I didn't

This recipe was WAY too runny. After the outline I piped ran over the edge of the cake I was decorating, I ended up having to add much more sugar just to thicken it up, but what I think it actually needed was cornstarch... which is in an older recipe I didn't bother to go looking for, figuring royal icing was simple enough they'd all be similar. Probably could have used far less of the egg whites, too. I literally ended up scraping off the first attempt and painting/dabbing it on with toothpicks.
First time came out pretty well for not knowing what I was doing! Easy enough, first time I’ve ever made my own powdered sugar, pasteurized eggs, and icing, and all in one night!
Very simple to make in my stand mixer. Let's see how we'll it sets up on the cookies but it looks very promising!!
Who measures in quarts for powdered sugar!?! 2qt=8C=64oz=4lbs of powdered sugar. Just say "4lbs of Confectionery sugar, instead of "2qts"...
This recipe makes a great sugar cookie icing. After piping, the icing will smooth itself out. It was fun to play with and I’d make it again!

I loved this icing! The texture was perfect and tasted very good! Although to get the texture I wanted it took a while to beat but since it a meringue like icing that is expected. Other than that, I would definitely recommend! This icing also makes it super easy to decorate cookies with!
Yum in my yum
